script: セイバールート十四日目-09
title: セイバールート十四日目-09

pages.ja:
慣れない一日は慌ただしく過ぎていった。
セイバーは最後まで声をあげて笑わず、俺も心から笑えるコトなどなかった。
pages.jaRuby:
慣れない一日は慌ただしく過ぎていった。
セイバーは最後まで声をあげて笑わず、俺も心から笑えるコトなどなかった。
pages.en:
The unfamiliar day passes in a rush.

Saber never once laughs aloud, and nothing happens that allows me to laugh from the heart.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The unusual day goes by quickly.
Saber never laughed nor could I laugh from my heart.

pages.ja:
印象に残るほど楽しい出来事があった訳ではないし、 後悔するほどつまらない時間ではなかった。
言ってしまえば、なんでもないコトだったのだ。
これなら屋敷に残って、道場でセイバーと剣の鍛錬をしていた方がセイバーは喜んだかもしれない。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Nothing is so delightful that it leaves a lasting impression, but neither is the time so dull that I regret it.

To put it plainly, nothing much happens at all.

Saber might have enjoyed herself more if we had stayed at the manor and trained with swords in the dojo.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s not like there was any memorable moments nor were it so boring that I regret doing it.
To be frank, this was nothing.
Saber might have been happier if we’d stayed at the mansion and trained together.

pages.ja:
それでも、この一日は悪くなかった。
つまらなくとも面白くなくとも、セイバーをこうして連れ回した事を、俺は最後に誇れる筈だ。
……戦いが終わって、何もかも元通りになった後。
セイバーと過ごした時間が戦いだけだったなんて、そんなのは空しすぎる。
pages.jaRuby:
それでも、この一日は悪くなかった。

……戦いが終わって、何もかも元通りになった後。
セイバーと過ごした時間が戦いだけだったなんて、そんなのは空しすぎる。
pages.en:
Even so, the day is not a bad one.

However dull or unremarkable it may have been, I will be able to take pride in having dragged Saber around like this.

…After the war ends and everything returns to the way it was,

the thought that every moment Saber and I shared was spent fighting would be unbearably empty.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But today wasn’t bad.
It wasn’t fun or boring, but I can be proud of it in the end.
…After the battle is over and everything goes back to normal…
It would be too sad if all the time Saber and I had was spent fighting.

pages.ja:
たとえ愚かな行為でも、戦い以外の時間を重ねなくては彼女がここにいる意味がない。
だから、今は胸を張っていい。
……終わりは近い。
全てが終わって、もう戦う必要がなくなった時。
こんなコトもあった、とセイバーが思い出してくれるなら、それは十分に誇れる事なんだから
pages.jaRuby:

だから、今は胸を張っていい。
……終わりは近い。
全てが終わって、もう戦う必要がなくなった時。
こんなコトもあった、とセイバーが思い出してくれるなら、それは十分に誇れる事なんだから
pages.en:
Foolish or not, unless we share time outside of battle, there is no meaning in her being here.

So for now, I can hold my head high.

…The end is near.

When everything is over and there is no longer any need to fight,

if Saber remembers that once, there was a day like this, then I will have done something worthy of pride—
pages.mirrorMoon:
Even if it’s something stupid, she has to spend some time not fighting, or there’s no point in her being here.
So I can be proud of myself for now.
…The end is near.
When everything comes to an end and when there’s no more need to fight…
If Saber will remember this moment and remember that this happened, that alone is enough for me to be proud of.

pages.ja:
帰り道は徒歩だった。
バスで帰ろうとした矢先、
「帰りは歩いていきましょう」
とセイバーが提案した為である。
pages.jaRuby:

「帰りは歩いていきましょう」
とセイバーが提案した為である。
pages.en:
We walk home.

Just as I was about to suggest the bus, Saber said,

“Let us return on foot.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
We go home on foot.
Because Saber said,
“Let us walk home.”
…Just as I decided to go home by bus.

pages.ja:
風が出ていた。
鮮やかな夕日が橋を赤く照らしている。
「
あ」
セイバーは何かに気が付いたのか、足を止めて川の中程を見つめていた。
その視線の先にあるのは、ちょっとした瓦礫の山だ。

pages.en:
The wind has risen.

A brilliant sunset paints the bridge red.

“—Ah.”

Saber notices something and stops, staring toward the middle of the river.

A low mound of wreckage lies in the water.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There’s some wind now.
The vivid setting sun is lighting the bridge red.
“Oh.”
Saber notices something and stops.
She is watching a mountain of rubble.

pages.ja:
瓦礫の山、といっても高さはない。
水面より少し低い程度に積み重なった鉄骨やら何やらが、川の流れをわずかだけ歪めている。
事情は知らないが、ずいぶん昔に停泊していた船が沈没したとかで破片が流れ、溜まって山になったのだそうだ。
美観を損ねるので撤去してほしい、という近隣住民の要望が、もう長いコト続いているらしい。

pages.en:
It is not much of a mound.

Steel beams and other debris are heaped just below the surface, distorting the river's current only slightly.

I do not know the details. Supposedly a ship moored here sank long ago, and its scattered remains accumulated in one place.

For years, local residents have demanded that the eyesore be removed.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s not that tall even though it’s a ‘mountain’ of rubble.
Steel frames and the likes are piled right up to the water surface and are slightly distorting the flow of the river.
I don’t know why, but it seems like a ship sank or something, and pieces of it flowed into a mountain.
I heard the local residents have been demanding its removal for a long time since it damages the beautiful sight.

pages.ja:
「？ なんだよセイバー。アレが気になったのか？」
「いえ、まだ残っていたのかと。アレの原因は私ですから。前回の戦いで水上戦を余儀なくされ、ここで宝具を使ってしまった。
被害は川を干上がらせただけでしたが、運悪く停泊していた船を巻き込んでしまったのです」
pages.jaRuby:
「？ なんだよセイバー。アレが気になったのか？」
「いえ、まだ残っていたのかと。アレの原因は私ですから。前回の戦いで水上戦を余儀なくされ、ここで宝具を使ってしまった。
被害は川を干上がらせただけでしたが、運悪く停泊していた船を巻き込んでしまったのです」
pages.en:
“Hm? What is it, Saber? Something about that wreckage?”

“No. I was surprised that it remains. I am responsible for it. During the previous war, I was forced into a battle upon the water and used my Noble Phantasm here.

“The river merely ran dry, but unfortunately, a moored ship was caught in the attack.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…? What’s wrong, Saber? Did that catch your attention?”
“No, I was noticing that it still remains because I was the cause of it. I used the Noble Phantasm here, having fought on water in the previous war.
The only damage was that the river dried up, but I also destroyed the ship that was unfortunately anchored there.”

pages.ja:
「はあ
？ 巻き込んだって、まさかエクスカリバーにか！？」
「そ、そうなのですが、幸い乗客はいませんでしたし、被害も大きくなかったんです。川だって今では元通りですし、そう怒らなくともいいではありませんか。
……私だって、その、反省しているのですから」
pages.jaRuby:
「はあ
？ 巻き込んだって、まさかエクスカリバーにか！？」
「そ、そうなのですが、幸い乗客はいませんでしたし、被害も大きくなかったんです。川だって今では元通りですし、そう怒らなくともいいではありませんか。
……私だって、その、反省しているのですから」
pages.en:
“What—? You hit a ship with Excalibur!?”

“Y-yes, but fortunately there were no passengers, and the damage was not extensive. The river itself has long since recovered. Surely there is no need to be so angry.

“…I regret what happened as well.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh? You mean Excalibur!?”
“Y-Yes. But fortunately, nobody was on board and the damage was minimal. The river is back to normal, so you should not get so mad.
…I regret it as well.”

pages.ja:
「………………」
……気をつけよう。
エクスカリバーを使う時は、せめてこれぐらい広いところじゃないとシャレにならない。
pages.jaRuby:
「………………」
……気をつけよう。
エクスカリバーを使う時は、せめてこれぐらい広いところじゃないとシャレにならない。
pages.en:
“………………”

…I had better remember this.

When Saber uses Excalibur, even an open space as wide as this barely qualifies as safe.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
…I should watch out.
I have to take care to only use Excalibur in an open place like this.

pages.ja: 「シロウ……？ まだ怒っていますか？」
pages.jaRuby: 「シロウ……？ まだ怒っていますか？」
pages.en: “Shirou…? Are you still angry?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Shirou…? Are you still mad?”

pages.ja:
「え？ いや、別に怒ってない。ただびっくりしただけだ。あとはまあ、前回の名残ってけっこうあるんだなって。
中央公園の荒れ野に比べたら、川の瓦礫なんて問題じゃないだろ。ま、船の持ち主は災難だったとは思うが」
pages.jaRuby:
「え？ いや、別に怒ってない。ただびっくりしただけだ。あとはまあ、前回の名残ってけっこうあるんだなって。
中央公園の荒れ野に比べたら、川の瓦礫なんて問題じゃないだろ。ま、船の持ち主は災難だったとは思うが」
pages.en:
“What? No, I'm not angry. I was surprised, that's all. And I suppose I hadn't realized how many traces of the last war are still here.

“Compared with the wasteland in Central Park, some debris in the river is nothing. Though I do feel sorry for whoever owned the ship.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Eh? No, I’m not mad. I was just surprised. And I was just thinking how many traces there are from the last war.
The rubble in the river shouldn’t be a problem compared to the wasteland in that park. Well, I guess it was unfortunate for the owner of that ship.”

pages.ja: 「それはご安心を。船の持ち主には保険が下りたと切嗣が言っていましたし、もともと緩衝材にするつもりで船を止めさせたのですから。船体を壁にみたてて、宝具の威力を削いだのですね」
pages.jaRuby: 「それはご安心を。船の持ち主には保険が下りたと切嗣が言っていましたし、もともと緩衝材にするつもりで船を止めさせたのですから。船体を壁にみたてて、宝具の威力を削いだのですね」
pages.en: “You need not. Kiritsugu told me the owner's insurance paid for the loss. Besides, he had arranged for the ship to remain there precisely as a buffer. He used its hull as a wall to diminish the force of my Noble Phantasm.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Please do not worry as Kiritsugu said the owner had insurance. He parked the ship there as a buffer, so he used the ship as a wall to reduce the power of the Noble Phantasm.”

pages.ja: 「……なんだ。じゃあ初めから承知で船を壊したってコトか」
pages.jaRuby: 「……なんだ。じゃあ初めから承知で船を壊したってコトか」
pages.en: “…Oh. So you knew from the beginning that the ship would be destroyed.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…Oh. So you destroyed the ship knowing it was there?”

pages.ja:
「承知していた訳ではありませんっ。アレは切嗣が私に黙って用意していた物です。
……そうですね。切嗣には戦いの流れが読めていたのでしょう。船を用意する前もその後も、一言も口にしなかったので気が付きませんでしたが」
pages.jaRuby:
「承知していた訳ではありませんっ。アレは切嗣が私に黙って用意していた物です。
……そうですね。切嗣には戦いの流れが読めていたのでしょう。船を用意する前もその後も、一言も口にしなかったので気が付きませんでしたが」
pages.en:
“I did not know! Kiritsugu prepared it without telling me.

“…I see. He must have anticipated the course of the battle. He said nothing before or after arranging it, so I never realized.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I did not know! Kiritsugu prepared it without telling me.
…I think Kiritsugu knew how the battle would turn out. I did not notice since he never said anything before or after he prepared the ship.”

pages.ja:
そうして、懐かしそうにセイバーは川を見下ろした。
キラキラと夕日を反射させる水面。
川から吹き上がってくる風はやや強く、セイバーの髪を揺らしていた。
pages.jaRuby:
そうして、懐かしそうにセイバーは川を見下ろした。
キラキラと夕日を反射させる水面。
川から吹き上がってくる風はやや強く、セイバーの髪を揺らしていた。
pages.en:
Saber gazes down at the river with something like nostalgia.

The setting sun glitters upon the water.

The wind rising from the river is strong enough to stir her hair.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Saber looks down at the river yearningly.
The water surface reflects the sunset.
The wind coming from the river is a bit strong and flutters Saber’s hair.

pages.ja:
……その姿が、あまりにも綺麗だったからか。
「セイバー。今日は楽しかったか」
このままセイバーが消えてしまいそうな不安に駆られて、訊かなくてもいい事を訊いていた。
pages.jaRuby:
……その姿が、あまりにも綺麗だったからか。
「セイバー。今日は楽しかったか」
このままセイバーが消えてしまいそうな不安に駆られて、訊かなくてもいい事を訊いていた。
pages.en:
…Perhaps it is because she looks so beautiful.

“Saber. Did you enjoy today?”

A sudden fear seizes me that she may disappear as I watch. I ask the question though there is no need.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Is it because she looks so beautiful like that?
“Saber, did you have fun today?”
I was assaulted by a sudden fear that Saber might just disappear, and I ask something I don’t need to ask.

pages.ja:
「はい？ なにか言いましたか、シロウ？」
「言った。今日は楽しかったか、訊いた」
……息を呑む。
セイバーはきょとん、と目を開いたあと。
pages.jaRuby:
「はい？ なにか言いましたか、シロウ？」
「言った。今日は楽しかったか、訊いた」
……息を呑む。
セイバーはきょとん、と目を開いたあと。
pages.en:
“Hm? Did you say something, Shirou?”

“I did. I asked whether you enjoyed today.”

…I hold my breath.

Saber blinks at me in surprise. Then—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh? Did you say something, Shirou?”
“Yeah. I asked you if you had fun today.”
…She gasps.
Saber opens her eyes in amazement.

pages.ja:
「そうですね。新鮮でないと言えば嘘になります」
もう、それが起き得ない事のように。
憧れを含んだ声で、そう言った。
pages.jaRuby:
「そうですね。新鮮でないと言えば嘘になります」
もう、それが起き得ない事のように。
憧れを含んだ声で、そう言った。
pages.en:
“Yes. I would be lying if I said it held nothing new for me.”

She speaks with longing,

as though such a day could never happen again.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes. I would be lying if I said this was not new to me.”
She says so in a voice of hope.
As if such a thing will never happen again.

pages.ja:
「
」
……だから、答えなど分かっていたのだ。
あと出来る事といえば、そうか、と頷いて帰るだけ。
それだけなら、まだ
取り返しがつく筈だ。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
……だから、答えなど分かっていたのだ。
あと出来る事といえば、そうか、と頷いて帰るだけ。
それだけなら、まだ
取り返しがつく筈だ。
pages.en:
“—”

…I already knew her answer.

All that remains is to nod, say *I see,* and continue home.

If I do only that, perhaps nothing will have passed beyond repair.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
…I knew what her answer would be.
All I can do now is nod and just go home.
Everything can return to the way it wasjust like that.

pages.ja:
「そうか」
セイバーの目を見据えたまま頷いて。
「ならまた行こう。こんなの、別に今回限りってワケじゃないんだから」
おそらく、取り返しのつかなくなる言葉を口にした。
pages.jaRuby:
「そうか」
セイバーの目を見据えたまま頷いて。
「ならまた行こう。こんなの、別に今回限りってワケじゃないんだから」
おそらく、取り返しのつかなくなる言葉を口にした。
pages.en:
“I see.”

I nod without looking away from her.

“Then we'll do it again. There's no reason this has to be the only time.”

The words I speak may carry us past the point of no return.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see.”
I nod, looking at Saber.
“Then let’s go again. It’s not like this has to be the last time.”
And I say something I won’t be able to take back.

pages.ja:
「
」
セイバーの表情が固まる。
……俺の言いたい事が分かったのだろう。
彼女は俺をはっきりと見据えたまま、静かに首を横に振った。
二度目はない、と。
これは、今日だけの間違いだと言うかのように。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
セイバーの表情が固まる。
……俺の言いたい事が分かったのだろう。
彼女は俺をはっきりと見据えたまま、静かに首を横に振った。
二度目はない、と。
これは、今日だけの間違いだと言うかのように。
pages.en:
“—”

Saber's expression freezes.

…She understands what I mean.

Meeting my eyes without wavering, she slowly shakes her head.

There will be no second time.

As if today were an error that could be permitted only once.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
Saber freezes.
…She must have realized what I want to say.
She shakes her head, looking directly at me.
As if saying there won’t be a next time.
As if this mistake is only for today.

pages.ja:
「
それは、何故」
セイバーの返答なんて分かっている。
それでも、思った通りのセイバーの答えに納得がいかなくて聞き返した。
pages.jaRuby:
「
それは、何故」
セイバーの返答なんて分かっている。
それでも、思った通りのセイバーの答えに納得がいかなくて聞き返した。
pages.en:
“—Why?”

I know what she will say.

Even so, I cannot accept the answer I know is coming, and force her to say it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Why?”
I know Saber’s answer.
But I ask, not liking the answer I expect.

pages.ja:
「何故も何もない。サーヴァントは戦う為に存在する者です。今日のような行為は、自らの存在を否定する事になる。
シロウが休憩すべきだと判断したから従いましたが、もうこの先は、体を休める必要はないでしょう。
残る敵は少ない。シロウが命じるなら、今すぐにでもランサーを捜し出したいほどですが」
pages.jaRuby:
「何故も何もない。サーヴァントは戦う為に存在する者です。今日のような行為は、自らの存在を否定する事になる。
シロウが休憩すべきだと判断したから従いましたが、もうこの先は、体を休める必要はないでしょう。
残る敵は少ない。シロウが命じるなら、今すぐにでもランサーを捜し出したいほどですが」
pages.en:
“There is no question of why. Servants exist to fight. To spend a day as we have today is to deny my own existence.

“I obeyed because you judged that we required rest. But from this point forward, there will be no further need to recuperate.

“Few enemies remain. If you ordered it, I would gladly begin searching for Lancer this very instant.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I do not even need to explain. Servants exist to fight. A day like today is merely denying my own existence.
I obeyed since you decided to take a rest, but I believe resting should not be necessary from now on.
There are only a few enemies left. I would like to start searching for Lancer right now if you would order me to…”

pages.ja:
闘志の籠もった目で見つめてくる。
命令さえあればこの場で戦いに赴くのに、とセイバーは言っている。
それが。
今まで納得のいかなかった部分に、火をつけてしまった。
pages.jaRuby:
闘志の籠もった目で見つめてくる。
命令さえあればこの場で戦いに赴くのに、とセイバーは言っている。
それが。
今まで納得のいかなかった部分に、火をつけてしまった。
pages.en:
She looks at me with battle burning in her eyes.

Give the command, she says, and she will leave for combat here and now.

And that—

sets fire to everything about her I could never accept.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She looks at me with eyes full of fire.
Saber is saying she will start fighting right now if I order it.
That…
…Causes me to get mad about all the things I can’t approve of.

pages.ja:
「
なんだよそれ。そんなに戦いたいのか、おまえは」
「当然でしょう。戦えば戦うほど聖杯に近づくのです。
私にとって、戦闘は何よりも優先すべき事です。それはシロウとて判っている筈ですが」
pages.jaRuby:
「
なんだよそれ。そんなに戦いたいのか、おまえは」
「当然でしょう。戦えば戦うほど聖杯に近づくのです。
私にとって、戦闘は何よりも優先すべき事です。それはシロウとて判っている筈ですが」
pages.en:
“—What the hell is that supposed to mean? Do you really want to fight that badly?”

“Do not presume so much. What could a man like you possibly understand of me?

“You have no right to intrude upon my heart.

“You tell me not to fight? What right has an immature Master who cannot survive without my protection? Save such delusions until you are capable of fighting alone.

“—Though of course, that day will never come.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Do not be so conceited. What makes you think you understand me?
You have no right to invade me.
Do not fight? What are you saying when you need me to protect you? Please, give me that nonsense after you are able to fight on your own.
Humph. I do not think that will ever occur.”

“They are delusions. You tell me to consider myself? The same charge applies to you, Shirou.

“You attach no weight to your own life.

“You call me mistaken, but it is you who has lost sight of something fundamental.

“…To place others before oneself is the thinking of the dead.

“How dare a great fool who does not know the worth of his own life speak to me in such terms?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It is nonsense. Think about myself? That goes for you as well.
You do not consider your life.
You say I am mistaken, but you are even more mistaken.
…Only corpses consider others more important than themselves.
How can a fool who does not even know the value of his own life address me so?”

“Have I offended you? Then I am willing to dissolve our contract. You have no need of the Grail in any case.

“I will defeat the remaining Masters and obtain it alone.

“…If battle disgusts you so greatly, you may hide somewhere far away.”

“Did I annoy you? Then I will not mind if you dissolve your contract with me. You do not need the Holy Grail anyway.
I will defeat the remaining Masters by myself and obtain the Holy Grail myself.
…If you do not wish to fight, you can go and hide somewhere far away.”

震える声で問う。

“Saber. Do you really mean that?”

My voice trembles.

My teeth chatter because I am suppressing more emotion than I knew I possessed.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Saber. Are you serious?”
I ask with a trembling voice.
My teeth are chattering because I’m suppressing my emotion.

“Naturally. My sole purpose is the Holy Grail. Everything else is superfluous.

“—You are no exception, Shirou.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course. My only goal is the Holy Grail. Everything else is unnecessary.
You are no exception, Shirou.”

I cannot contain the emotion.

I shout words that sound like an excuse for flight, then turn and run from Saber.

Her figure recedes.

For one instant—

I think I see Saber standing there in a daze.

But I can’t stop my emotions.
I yell what sounds like an excuse and run away from Saber.
I get away from her.
But, for a moment.
I think I see Saber standing there absent-mindedly.

“Damn it. Damn it—damn it…!”

I run.

I do not know what hurts or why I am angry. I abandon myself to the storm and run.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Dammit, dammit, dammit…!”
I run.
I keep running, not knowing what’s so vexing or maddening.

…If only it were that simple.

If Saber had merely made me angry, I could lash out like an idiot and be done with it.

But that is not the source of this fury.

I am not angry with Saber.

I am running and running, refusing myself even time to breathe, because I am furious with my own helplessness.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…No, it would be easy if I could do that.
If I was just angry at Saber, I could just take it out on something.
But that’s not the cause of this fury.
It’s not
just
Saber that I’m mad at.
It’s so vexing, and I keep running so hard because I hate how weak I am.

”

I spit out the words and nearly stumble beneath the weight of regret.

…What had she revealed in that moment?

Her voice seemed to sever us, yet at the same time, it trembled on the verge of tears.

Looking back, perhaps those words alone had been true.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…! Damn it! You idiot, I don’t understand…!”
I spit that out, then regret it so much that I almost fall.
…What was it about?
Her voice like a farewell sounded like she was crying.
Come to think of it, maybe those words were the only honest thing she said.

A voice mingling expectation, disappointment, and desperate appeal.

—Then—

which of us betrayed the other? Which of us was betrayed?

Those words murmured with her head hung.
A voice of hope, disappointment, and wishes.
Then…
Who was the betrayer, and who was betrayed?

I rush into my room and slam the sliding door.

Then I fall spread-eagled upon the floor.

Even standing is too much effort.

For now, I want only to lie here and lose myself in sleep.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I run into my room and shut the door.
I collapse.
I don’t want to stand up.
I just want to lie down and go to sleep.

My heart feels ready to burst, and my lungs claw frantically for air.

I sprinted all the way from the bridge without stopping. Of course my body has reached its limit.

My feelings still demand that I run, but my body has begun shouting at me to calm down.

But my body is still burning.
My heart feels like it’s splitting open and my lungs are desperate for air.
I ran full speed from the bridge to here. My body must be exhausted.
I haven’t run enough emotionally, but my body is telling me to calm down.

I draw a deep breath and let it out.

I slowly calm down.
I take a deep breath and let it out.

All that fills my head is the question of why I was so enraged.

…I cannot save Saber.

That is what hurts. That is why I am angry with myself.

I can do nothing.

I swore I would make her smile.

I decided I would protect her. Yet I remain incapable of either, and the knowledge fills me with helpless rage.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I can’t save Saber.
That fact is so vexing that I was angry at myself.
I can’t do anything.
I promised to make her laugh.
I promised to protect her, but I can’t do anything. That makes me furious.

“…But what am I supposed to do? Until Saber wants happiness for herself, nothing anyone else says will matter.”

That was why I made an effort so unlike me—to help Saber discover happiness of her own.

She called even that meaningless, then named me a great fool for good measure.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…But what can I do? It’s useless for anyone to say anything if Saber herself doesn’t want happiness.”
That’s why I tried hard, so she’d be able to find her own happiness.
But she told me that was meaningless, and on top of that, she called me a fool.

“A great fool who doesn't know the worth of his own life…”

…What does she expect me to do with that?

I value my own life. I have no desire to throw it away.

“A fool who doesn’t even know the value of his own life, huh?”
…What can I do when she says that?
I value my life as well and I don’t want to do anything that might endanger it.
